 Edited by Nitesh Dubey / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 20, 2026, 16:41 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium

 Print Hardik Pandya (Image: IANS) Punjab Kings head coach Ricky Ponting believes the addition of Hardik Pandya has given the franchise a well-rounded squad, with the all-rounder bringing greater balance and flexibility ahead of IPL 2027. Punjab made a major move in the trade window by securing Pandya from Mumbai Indians in exchange for India pacer Arshdeep Singh , with the deal completed at Rs 18 crore for each player. The trade marks a significant change for both franchises, with Pandya ending his second stint at Mumbai Indians to join Punjab, while Arshdeep moves to the five-time IPL champions after eight seasons with PBKS. Watch Glenn Phillips on India's bowling attack, Bumrah's threat, pitch conditions & New Zealand's strategy With the retention deadline now behind them, Punjab have retained 19 players and released six, choosing to keep the core of their squad together as they prepare for the next three-year cycle. Ponting believes Pandya's presence, alongside several other versatile players, will give the team multiple options with both bat and ball. Speaking to JioStar, the former Australia captain explained the franchise's retention strategy and how the new addition has strengthened their squad. 'We've got a very well-rounded squad': Ponting on Hardik Pandya's arrival 
 Ponting said Punjab were keen to retain the majority of their existing players while making selective changes to improve the squad. He highlighted the number of all-rounders available to the franchise, believing their presence would help cover different combinations and playing conditions. "I've been really conscious of trying to keep the majority of our players together through this three-year cycle, leading into another mega auction next year. So we've decided to release six players going into the IPL (2027) and have retained 19," Ponting told JioStar. Join conversation

 Explaining the value Pandya brings to the side, Ponting said: "We've obviously brought in, through trade, Hardik Pandya, and traded out Arshdeep Singh. We've got a very well-rounded squad. Obviously, there's been a lot of talk about how many all-rounders we've got in our group. "With Hardik coming in and Marco Jansen, Marcus Stoinis , Azmatullah (Omarzai), (Suryansh) Shedge, Shashank (Singh), Cooper Connolly, there are a lot of all-rounders there. "It will hold us in really good stead. We've got a lot of bases covered there as far as spin bowling all-rounders and fast bowling all-rounders are concerned," he added.
